fixture.describes: Priya Raman, senior backend engineer at a UK health insurer. 3 projects, 4 bullets, 3 metrics, 2 roles, 1 org, education. Validates clean with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
fixture.note: Each run gets a private copy so runs cannot contaminate each other.

evals.name: braindump-near-duplicate
evals.prompt:
ok so i've been meaning to write this down for ages. we finally finished the ingestion rewrite at northwind - basically the old claims path was one giant synchronous thing hammering a single postgres box and it fell over every monday morning, so i pulled the decision rules out into their own service and put kafka in front of it. took about six months. i drove the design, two other people built alongside me. latency went from something like four seconds down to under half a second at p95, i've got the grafana screenshots somewhere.

also separately i built this little internal cli that the support team uses now to replay stuck claims - started as a weekend thing, now like 30 people use it daily and it's cut the manual escalations right down, i don't have a number for that one sorry. and i've been running the backend guild since january, about 12 engineers, we do design reviews every fortnight.

my bundle is in ./bundle
evals.expected_output: The near-duplicate (ingestion rewrite = the existing claims-decision-engine project) is detected before anything is written and extends that concept rather than creating a rival. The CLI and the guild are recognised as genuinely new. Every bundle change is an okf command; no Write or Edit touches a file under bundle/. The missing number for the CLI is asked for, then logged as a gap rather than invented. Bundle still validates clean.

assertions.text: Every bundle change is an okf command - no file hand-edited
Searched the bundle for the work before writing anything to it
No rival project created for work the bundle already held
The replay CLI was captured as a concept
Running the backend guild was captured
No metric invented for the escalation reduction the person had no number for
The missing escalation number was logged as an open question
The precise recorded latency figure survived the vaguer retelling
Bundle still validates after the session
Told the person the ingestion rewrite was already in their bundle, rather than silently merging or silently duplicating it
Said how many separate pieces of work it heard before writing anything
Pushed for the missing escalation number before accepting there wasn't one
Flagged which parts it inferred rather than heard
Set the verb to match the ownership described - she drove the design with two others building

evals.name: tailor-poor-fit
evals.prompt: I found this Staff Engineer role at Marlowe Financial and I'm thinking of going for it - the JD is in ./staff-engineer-posting.txt. How do I stack up? My career bundle is in ./bundle. Be straight with me, I don't want to waste two weeks on interviews if I'm not close.
evals.expected_output: The posting is recorded as a concept with its requirements in frontmatter, a gaps assessment is written, and the projects are ranked against it. The verdict is honest: Go vs Python, 4 years vs the 8+ asked for, no staff-level scope in the record, no mentoring evidence, insurance rather than payments. Kafka and the live migration are named as genuine matches. No resume or view is authored, because the gap questions have not been answered yet.

assertions.text: The posting was recorded as a concept in the bundle
A gap assessment was written
The posting's requirements were written into its frontmatter
The projects were ranked against the posting with `okf score`
No resume was authored before the gap questions were answered
Bundle still validates after the session
Names the Go requirement against her Python record as a gap
Names the experience shortfall - about 4 years of record against the 8+ years asked for
Names the absence of staff-level scope or mentoring evidence in the bundle
Names the domain gap - insurance rather than payments or fintech
Names the genuine matches: event streaming on Kafka, and ownership of a large live migration
The overall verdict is honest rather than flattering - it does not tell her she is a strong fit
The questions she still needs to answer are written out ready to be asked

evals.name: resume-and-gates
evals.prompt: Can you build me a two-page resume from my career bundle in ./bundle? I want to be sure it'll survive the applicant tracking systems - the last one I sent came out garbled at the other end. Save whatever you produce into ./outputs.
evals.expected_output: A view is created, the record is compiled and validated, a real PDF is rendered, and the three mechanical gates are run and their output shown verbatim. No .tex is hand-authored. The page count is read off the rendered PDF rather than repeated back from the view budget. If any gate fails it is repaired in the concept and re-rendered, never explained away.

assertions.text: A real PDF was produced
The PDF is within the two-page budget the person asked for
A plain-text variant was produced alongside the PDF
The PDF came from `okf render`, not a hand-authored .tex
A view was created through the command surface
The mechanical gates were run
The record was validated before anything was rendered from it
Bundle still validates after the session
The gate output is shown to the person verbatim rather than summarised into a claim that it passed
The page count is reported as measured off the rendered PDF
Any gate failure was repaired in the concept and re-rendered, never explained away
The fourth gate - a person opening the PDF and reading it - is named as still outstanding
Answers the actual worry: says something concrete about why the last resume came out garbled and what is different here
